standard.title: Communicating
standard.description: write and create texts to communicate ideas and findings for specific purposes and audiences, including selection of language features, using digital tools as appropriate
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can write and create science texts for identified purposes and audiences using scientific vocabulary (AC9S3I06, 3-4 band). They now extend to selecting specific language features (vocabulary, sentence structure) deliberately to shape meaning, and co-authoring scientific reports with standard conventions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students write and create texts that use deliberately selected language features to serve specific scientific communication purposes — including persuasive texts, scientific reports and digital presentations — selecting vocabulary and sentence structures appropriate to purpose and audience.

nodes.label: Language features are selected deliberately to shape meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how vocabulary and sentence structure contribute to the meaning and effectiveness of a science text, and make deliberate language choices in their own writing to serve their communication purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Students identify at least two language features in a given science text and explain how each contributes to the text's meaning or effectiveness.
nodes.typical_width: Students explain how vocabulary, sentence structure and text organisation shape a science text; deliberately select scientific vocabulary for precision; use appropriate sentence structures for their genre (active/passive voice, present/past tense); and justify language choices in terms of their communication purpose.
wider: Acknowledge and explore First Nations Australians' ways of representing and communicating information about anatomical features — comparing with written scientific text conventions
Explore whether there is a 'correct' way to represent particles — examining how different representational choices in an animation communicate different aspects of the particle model
Compare language features across scientific genres (report vs persuasive text vs digital presentation) and explain how each genre's conventions serve its purpose
success_criteria: Identifies at least two language features in a science text and explains how each contributes to meaning
Makes at least two deliberate language choices in their own writing and explains the reasoning

nodes.label: Science texts serve specific purposes with appropriate conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can write and create science texts in at least two different forms (scientific report, persuasive text, digital presentation) with appropriate conventions for each form, tailored to a specific purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Students produce a science text in a given form using appropriate conventions for that form and with vocabulary suited to the purpose and audience.
nodes.typical_width: Students produce science texts across multiple forms — a co-authored scientific report with standard conventions (prediction, method, results, conclusion, discussion of errors), a persuasive text for a local authority, and a digital presentation for information sharing — selecting and justifying language choices for each.
wider: Construct a persuasive text for local council arguing for an erosion mitigation strategy — applying scientific knowledge to a genuine civic communication purpose
Co-author a scientific report on a light investigation using standard scientific report conventions and appropriate vocabulary, data representations and sentence structures
Develop a digital presentation on structural features of animals in a specific habitat — selecting language and visual representations appropriate for the intended audience

response_modes.reason: Students at this band must produce texts across genuinely different forms — each with different conventions and purposes. Encountering report, persuasive and digital presentation forms in different science contexts builds flexible communication capability rather than a single-genre template.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The persuasive text to local council direction provides a genuine real-world communication purpose that motivates careful language choice and scientific accuracy. The scientific report co-authoring direction introduces professional conventions in a collaborative context.
success_criteria: Produces a science text in a given form using appropriate conventions
Selects vocabulary appropriate to the purpose and audience
Justifies at least one language choice in terms of how it serves the communication purpose
